In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods for estimating genetic parameters and breeding values of dairy cattle using test-day (TD), rather than 305-d, records.
the use of TD records to improve the accuracy of genetic evaluations for milk, fat and protein yields and somatic cell scores in dairy cattle.
the development and evaluation of a test-day model for dairy cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of TD models with autoregression for short-term environmental effects resulted in the best genetic evaluation and the best prediction of genetic merit of animals.
TD models can be used to obtain more accurate genetic evaluations than 305-d models, but the differences in genetic evaluation accuracy are small.
the ARs model is the best model to be used to select dairy cows for higher milk, protein, and fat yields and for lower somatic cell scores.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ARs and A-Re models are better than the 305-d lactations model for genetic evaluation of Holstein dairy cattle for milk, fat and protein yields and somatic cell scores.
the ARs model is recommended for use in the Canadian Holstein genetic evaluation system.
the TD models with autoregressions were superior to a 305-d lactations model and the CS model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

genetic evaluation of dairy cattle using TD records with a first-order auto-regressive covariance structure for TD residuals or short-term TD environmental effects results in greater genetic improvement in milk, fat, protein, and SCS than genetic evaluation of dairy cows using 305-d milk records.
the TD models with autoregression covariance structures are better than the 305-d lactations model.
the TD models with ARs and A-Re models can be used to select animals that have a higher genetic merit for milk, fat and protein yields, as well as SCS than the 305-d models.
